title: An updated protocol for in vitro bovine embryo production
protocol: Fill two, 2 L PYREX glass bottles with 0.9% sodium chloride.
Supplement the 0.9% sodium chloride solution with 1× antibiotic-antimycotic (ABAM) and mix.
Add the two, 2 L PYREX glass bottles containing 0.9% sodium chloride with ABAM to the insulated cooler.
Add a strainer to the insulated cooler.
Add latex or nitrile gloves to the insulated cooler.
Drive to an abattoir to collect heifer or cow ovaries.
Warm pre-made oocyte collection medium in a water bath set to 38.5°C, two hours before use.
Plate and equilibrate oocyte maturation medium minimally two hours before use.
Sterilely add 500 μl oocyte maturation media (OMM) into the desired number of wells of 4-well Nunc™ plates.
Completely cover each well with mineral oil using a transfer pipette.
Transfer OMM Nunc™ plate(s) to a humidified incubator set at 38.5°C with 5% CO2.
Sterilely add 50 μl drops of OMM for desired number of times in a 60 mm petri dish.
Add mineral oil using a transfer pipette until each drop is fully covered.
Transfer OMM petri dish(es) to a humidified incubator set at 38.5°C with 5% CO2.
Plate and equilibrate wash dishes containing OMM minimally two hours before use.
Add ∼3 mL of OMM to a 35 mm petri dish using a transfer pipette.
Completely cover each dish with mineral oil using a transfer pipette.
Transfer the OMM wash dish(es) to a humidified, 5% CO2 incubator set at 38.5°C.
Rinse and strain unwashed ovaries using one of the 2 L PYREX glass bottles containing 0.9% sodium chloride with 1× ABAM.
Place unwashed ovaries into a strainer and pour an entire 2 L of 0.9% sodium chloride with 1× ABAM over them.
Repeat rinsing and straining in multiple groups if too many ovaries cannot fit in the strainer at one time.
Place rinsed ovaries directly into the bottom of the insulated cooler.
Pour 0.9% sodium chloride with ABAM over the ovaries to submerge them.
Transport the insulated cooler containing rinsed and submerged ovaries back to the laboratory.
Set out three reusable polypropylene low-form graduated beakers.
Sort the ovaries into high-quality, medium-quality, or low-quality categories based on their condition.
Sort ovaries based on the number of antral follicles.
Count individual ovaries until desired amount is reached and place them into individual reusable polypropylene low-form graduated beakers.
Pour new 0.9% sodium chloride with 1× ABAM on top of ovaries to submerge them.
Gently massage the ovaries.
Drain liquid down the sink to remove blood and contaminants.
Repeat massaging and rinsing until saline and antibiotic solution remains clear after massaging.
Add enough saline and antibiotic solution to fully submerge ovaries to prevent drying out.
Prepare a slashing station by placing 1 absorbent underpad, scissors, scalpel handle and blades, a 250 mL beaker, and a hemostat at each station.
Add 75 mL of oocyte collection media (OCM) to the beaker at each slashing station.
Attach a scalpel blade onto the scalpel handle carefully.
Clamp the utero-ovarian ligament using a hemostat so that the ovary is held tightly.
Trim away excess utero-ovarian ligament with scissors.
Rupture large follicles (≥ 8 mm) off to the side over an absorbent underpad.
Avoid getting follicular fluid in the OCM beaker when rupturing large follicles.
Slash any visible (antral) follicles < 8 mm over a top of the OCM filled beaker using a scalpel blade attached.
Make an ‘X’ incision over each follicle for individual attention.
Use a ‘checkerboard’ slashing technique by making several horizontal and vertical slashes into the ovary if there are many follicles present to save time.
Avoid slashing highly vascularized parts of the ovary or slash shallower to prevent bleeding as it can cause media clotting.
Submerge the slashed ovary still attached to the hemostat into the OCM beaker after each follicle has been slashed.
Swirl intensely and scrape all sides of the ovary up against the inside of the beaker.
Switch out scalpel blades whenever too much resistance is felt due to a dulling blade.
Transport the beaker containing COCs to a filtering station.
Attach a 100 μm strainer on top of an empty 50 mL conical tube.
Begin pouring liquid from the beaker slowly through the strainer.
Remove the strainer off the 50 mL conical tube when flow slows down.
Invert the strainer over an opened search plate.
Pipette up fresh, warmed OCM media and dispense it over the inverted cell strainer to displace COCs and tissue debris into the search plate.
Repeat the process until no more media is left in the beaker.
Use a transfer pipette to pipette up fresh OCM and rinse the beaker and go through the strainer one final time.
Fill the search plate with additional fresh OCM until it fills half of the search plate.
Move the search plate onto a plate warmer if more slashing is required or onto a glass microscope warmer attached to a stereomicroscope if ready to begin searching.
Fill a 35 mm petri dish halfway with fresh OCM (∼3 mL) using a transfer pipette when ready to begin searching.
Assemble a Drummond™ Captrol by attaching a hand-pulled, captrol glass tip onto the device.
Locate individual COCs and collect them, paying special attention to avoid debris in the captrol tip.
Periodically release collected COCs into the 35 mm OCM petri dish.
Repeat the process until the entire search plate has been searched.
Gently agitate the search plate to redistribute any potential leftover COCs.
Re-search the entire plate to ensure all COCs have been found.
Remove an OMM wash dish from the incubator and place it on the plate warmer.
Transfer all COCs from the 35 mm OCM dish into the OMM wash dish using a P200 pipette set to 200 μL with a gel-loading tip attached.
Gently move the OMM dish containing COCs in a circular motion to wash COCs and gather them in the middle of the dish.
Transfer COCs from the OMM wash into their final maturation plates using a Captrol device.
Place the final maturation 4-well Nunc™ or 60 mm petri dish on the plate warmer before transferring COCs.
Ensure COCs selected for maturation are of good quality: homogenous ooplasm, free of granulation, several layers of homogenous cumulus cells.
Collect 10 good quality COCs and transfer them into 1, 50 μl drop of OMM in a 60 mm petri dish covered in oil if using.
Repeat until all COCs are plated, and then place maturation plates back into a humidified 5% CO2 incubator set to 38.5°C.
Incubate for 21–24 h for maturation.
Prepare the sperm gradient in two 15 mL conical tubes by adding 4 mL BoviPure and 1 mL BoviDilute to make an 80% solution.
Prepare another 15 mL conical tube for the sperm gradient by adding 4 mL BoviPure and 6 mL BoviDilute to make a 40% solution.
Wrap each cap of the prepared tubes in parafilm.
Set the prepared tubes in a 38.5°C water bath.

Prepare fertilization plates or dishes in a humidified 38.5°C 5% CO2 incubator for Option 1 by filling a 35 mm petri dish with 2.8 mL SOF-FERT covered in oil, capable of fertilizing 120–200 COCs per dish.

Prepare fertilization plates or dishes in a humidified 38.5°C 5% CO2 incubator for Option 2 by filling each well of a 4-well Nunc™ plate with 500 μL SOF-FERT covered in oil, capable of fertilizing 20–50 COCs per well.
Prepare two SOF-FERT wash dishes halfway filled with SOF-FERT media using a transfer pipette for each set of up to 400 COCs.
Place the wash dishes in a humidified 38.5°C 5% CO2 incubator once made.
In one 15 mL conical tube, add 8–10 mL of SOF-FERT using a serological pipette for sperm pellet wash.
Place the conical tube in its stand.
Place the conical tube into a humidified 38.5°C 5% CO2 incubator with its cap off for gas exchange to equilibrate.
Add 12 mL HEPES-SOF per one set of COCs (≤400) using a serological pipette in a 15 mL conical tube.
Wrap the cap(s) in parafilm and set in a 38.5°C water bath.
Turn on microscope warmers.
Fill Citothaw with water and plug-in to warm.
Critical: The Citothaw must warm to and remain at 95°–98°F for proper semen thawing.
Turn on centrifuge and preheat it to 37°C.
Wipe down all countertops, tables, microscopes, and plate warmers with 70% ethanol.
Set out P1000 pipette with corresponding filtered tips on the countertop.
Set out P200 pipette with corresponding filtered tips on the countertop.
Set out P20 pipette with corresponding filtered tips on the countertop.
Set out several transfer pipettes on the countertop.
Place a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube on the countertop.
Prepare hemocytometer for use.
Set scissors on the countertop.
Place one 50 mL conical tube and one 15 mL conical tube on the countertop.
Set up two conical tube stands, one for 40/80% sperm gradient tubes and another for empty 50 and 15 mL conical tubes to collect semen and pelleted sperm respectively.
Place three empty 35 mm petri dishes on the plate warmer.
Remove a 15 mL conical tube of HEPES-SOF from the water bath.
Wipe down the removed conical tube with 70% ethanol.
Fill each 35 mm petri dish halfway with HEPES-SOF using a transfer pipette.
Place a 70 μm cell strainer in the first HEPES-SOF 35 mm petri dish.
Carefully handle the tubes containing the layered gradient to prevent mixing of the layers to maintain their integrity.
Wipe down the tubes containing the layered gradients and place them in a conical tube stand.
Layer 5 mL of the 40% solution on top of the first 80% tube using a transfer pipette slowly.
Repeat the layering process for the remaining 80% tube with 5 mL of the 40% solution.
Set the prepared gradients back into the water bath to remain warm.
Proceed to the liquid nitrogen tank with a warmed Citothaw set to 37°C.
Remove the desired amount of semen straws needed to fertilize COCs and place them immediately into the Citothaw.
Thaw the semen straws for 45 seconds in the Citothaw.
Remove the thawed straws of semen and wipe down with 70% ethanol.
Ensure that the semen straws and gloves are completely dry before proceeding.
Cut the tip end of the straw(s) with scissors.
Move the straw(s) over an opened 50 mL conical tube.
Cut the other end of the straw(s) under the cotton plug to expel contents into the conical tube.
Gently flick the straws against the sides of the conical tube to ensure all contents are expelled.
Hold the conical tube containing semen and extender in hand to keep it warm.
Remove 40/80% gradient tubes from water bath, wipe down with 70% ethanol, and set them in a conical tube rack.
Using a transfer pipette, slowly aspirate up the semen and extender.
Slowly deposit the semen and extender equally across the tops of both gradient tubes.
Prepare a warmed 40/80% gradient in a 15 mL conical tube.
Thaw bull semen at an appropriate temperature and layer it carefully on top of the gradient.
Place water in another 15 mL conical tube as balance for the other tube.
Ensure the final volume in each tube is identical before centrifugation.
Gently place each gradient with semen across from each other in the centrifuge for balancing.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 25 minutes at 37°C.
Note how COCs appear visually post-maturation.
Move COCs using gel-loading tips from maturation plates into the center of a 70 μm cell strainer within the first HEPES-SOF wash.
Wipe the outside of the gel-loading tip with a Kimwipe to remove oil before depositing COCs into the cell strainer.
Gently swirl COCs around in the first HEPES-SOF wash to wash them.
Move the filter containing COCs into the second HEPES-SOF wash and swirl again.
Repeat swirling COCs for third and final HEPES-SOF wash.
Remove the (2) 35 mm SOF-FERT wash dishes out of the incubator and place them onto the plate warmer.
Move the filter from HEPES-SOF into the first SOF-FERT wash, swirl.
Repeat for the second and final SOF-FERT wash.
Once the filter with COCs is in the last SOF-FERT wash, remove the final IVF plate(s) or dish(es).
Using a P200 set to 200 μL with gel-loading tip, pipette up desired number of COCs and transfer into 35 mm petri dish(es) for IVF.
Transfer COCs into each well in as little volume as possible if using a 4-well Nunc™ for IVF.
Return IVF plate(s) or dish(es) into the humidified 38.5°C 5% CO2 incubator.
Gently remove the (2) 15 mL conical tubes containing sperm to a conical tube rack.
Observe a visible sperm pellet at the bottom of conical tubes.
Aspirate the sperm pellet using a transfer pipette.
Transfer the aspirated sperm into a new 15 mL conical tube.
If no sperm pellet is observed, start the process again.
Repeat aspiration and transfer for any additional sperm pellets.
Combine all transferred sperm pellets in one 15 mL conical tube.
Add 7–9 mL of SOF-FERT to the tube containing the sperm pellets.
Gently mix the solution by performing a soft inversion twice.
Leave at least 1 mL of SOF-FERT behind and return it to the incubator.
Centrifuge the washed sperm pellet for 5 min at 300 × g at 37°C.
Carefully remove the tube containing the centrifuged sperm pellet.
Use a transfer pipette to slowly aspirate off the supernatant down to the 2 mL mark.
Switch to a P1000 set to 1,000 μL for better hand control to decrease the likelihood of disrupting the pellet.
Re-centrifuge at the same parameters if the sperm pellet moves or is no longer visible.
Pipette off excess liquid using the P1000 pipette until about 100 μL of SOF-FERT remains on top of the sperm pellet.
Agitate the tube to mix thoroughly.
Determine sperm concentration using a hemocytometer, optionally with a dilution in water to immobilize them for accurate cell counting.
Add sperm to the plate or dish containing fertilization media and COCs at a final concentration of 1 million sperm/1 mL fertilization media.
Use a P200 pipette set to 200 μL to collect COCs in fertilization media.
Add sperm into the dishes containing COCs.
Incubate all IVF dishes in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator at 38.5°C for 16–22 h.
Warm and equilibrate medium needed for embryo culture.
Prepare hypoxia chamber the evening prior if using tri-gas incubation is not available.
Thoroughly spray the hypoxia chamber with 70% ethanol.
Let the chamber air dry overnight in a clean space.
Prepare culture washes, final culture plates, and HEPES-SOF wash at least two hours before culturing.
Sterilize add a 50 μL drop of SOF-BE1 into the center of each well in 4-well Nunc™ plates.
Completely cover each drop with mineral oil using a transfer pipette.
Transfer the 4-well Nunc™ culture plate(s) to a humidified incubator or chamber set at 38.5°C filled with 5% CO2.
Cover each 50 µL culture drop with embryos, preferably holding and culturing 25 embryos per drop.
Use 4-well Nunc™ plates for embryo culture.
Sterilize two 35 mm petri dishes and add approximately 3 mL of SOF-BE1 using a transfer pipette to create wash plates.
Cover one of the SOF-BE1 wash dishes completely with mineral oil using a transfer pipette.
Transfer culture washes of SOF-BE1 to a humidified incubator set at 38.5°C and filled with 5% CO2.
Add 12 mL of HEPES-SOF to a 15 mL conical tube using a serological pipette.
Wrap each conical tube cap with parafilm.
Place the conical tubes in a 38.5°C water bath until use for IVC.
Denude presumptive zygotes from fertilization plates.
Remove a 15 mL HEPES-SOF conical tube from the water bath.
Disinfect the HEPES-SOF conical tube using 70% ethanol.
Use a transfer pipette to add approximately 3 mL of pre-warmed HEPES-SOF into three new 35 mm petri dishes placed on a plate warmer.
Add a 70 μM strainer into the second HEPES-SOF wash dish.
Remove fertilization plates containing presumptive zygotes from the incubator onto the warmer of the microscope or nearby plate warmer.
Gently swirl the dish to group presumptive zygotes close together in the middle for easier collection and pipetting.
Aspirate all presumptive zygotes using a P200 set to 200 μL with gel-loading pipette tips.
Wipe the outside of the pipette tip with a Kimwipe to remove oil from the fertilization plate or dish.
Release the presumptive zygotes into the first 35 mm dish containing HEPES-SOF and no strainer.
Gently swirl presumptive zygotes in the first HEPES-SOF wash dish to wash and collect them into the center of the dish.
Denude presumptive zygotes from cumulus cells using a P200 pipette set to 180 μL with a gel-loading tip.
Aspirate all presumptive zygotes in 180 μL volume and dispense into a sterile, 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Reset the P200 pipette to 150 μL for repeated pipetting.
Set a timer for 4 minutes.
Proceed to repeatedly pipette up and down continuously for 4 minutes.
Close the tube lid and vortex the 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing presumptive zygotes for 5 minutes.
Reset the P200 pipette to 180 μL with a gel-loading tip attached.
Aspirate all media containing presumptive zygotes from the 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Rinse the 1.5 mL centrifuge tube several times with additional HEPES-SOF to recover more presumptive zygotes.
Release denuded presumptive zygotes into the center of a 70 μm cell strainer in the second 35 mm petri dish containing HEPES-SOF and swirl to wash.
Move the strainer into the third HEPES-SOF wash and swirl again to wash.
Remove two 35 mm SOF-BEI petri dishes from the incubator, one with oil overlayed on top and one without oil.
Transfer the strainer with denuded presumptive zygotes from the final HEPES-SOF wash into the first SOF-BEI dish that does not contain oil and swirl to wash.
Use a P200 pipette set to 200 μL with gel-loading tip attached to aspirate denuded, presumptive zygotes and dispense them underneath the oil of the second 35 mm dish containing SOF-BE1.
Switch to using a Captrol (or other similar devices: Drummond™ Wiretrol™, The STRIPPER®, or mouth pipette) with a hand-pulled tip attached.
Aspirate up 20–30 presumptive zygotes from the last SOF-BE1 petri dish containing oil and dispense them into 50 μL culture drops of a 4-well Nunc™ plate.
Repeat the process until all adequate quality presumptive zygotes have been plated into culture drops in the 4-well Nunc™ plate.
Place the filled 4-well Nunc™ plate into a humidified incubator or hypoxia chamber containing tri-gas at 38.5°C for culturing.
Incubate embryos until desired endpoint or specific stages to evaluate development (i.e., day 2 post-IVF for cleavage, day 7 post-IVF for day 7 blastocysts, and day 8 post-IVF for day 8 blastocysts).
Turn on microscope warmers.
Wipe down all tables, microscopes, and plate warmers with 70% ethanol.
Record in a lab notebook the number of presumptive zygotes cultured.
Note how many did not cleave and remained as 1-cell (unfertilized).
Document how many embryos cleaved at least to the 2-cell stage.
Divide the number of embryos that cleaved by the total number of presumptive zygotes cultured to determine the cleavage rate.
Turn on microscope warmers.
Wipe down all tables, microscopes, and plate warmers with 70% ethanol.
Record in a lab notebook how many cleaved embryos progressed into a blastocyst.
Note the presence of the blastocoel cavity as a key feature for identifying a blastocyst.
Stage the blastocysts by distinguishing regular, expanded, hatching, or hatched blastocysts.
